subject: Judge D: judging→ready gate — block ready/claim until a task's wirings are judged (timeout fallback)
description:
Gate readiness on judgment. A task does NOT become claimable until its wirings are judged. Lifecycle: created → wiring → judging → ready → claimable. Part of the eager-judgment-lifecycle redesign.

DESIGN:
1. New lifecycle state 'judging' (or equivalent): a task whose candidate edges are not yet all judged is NOT ready, even if its blocking deps are done. Readiness derivation (daemon) gains the condition: all of this task's autowire candidate edges have judged:true (kept) or are pruned — i.e. no judged:false autowire edges remain.
2. The gate: start_task REJECTS a claim on a task still in 'judging' (edges unjudged). Extends the existing claim gate (which already requires worktree + claim).
3. FAILURE-MODE FALLBACK (fork 1 default — TUNABLE): if judgment stalls/fails (no judge, error, timeout), after a configurable timeout the task falls back to 'ready' with its still-unjudged edges FLAGGED (not silently trusted). The eager path is the happy path; the timeout fallback guarantees a judge hiccup can NEVER deadlock the graph. Surface the flag so a consuming agent knows the context is provisionally-unjudged.

TEST: a task with unjudged candidate edges is not_ready and start_task is rejected; once judged it becomes ready and claimable; a simulated judge stall flips it to ready-flagged after the timeout (no deadlock).

GUARDRAIL: do NOT let this deadlock — the timeout fallback is mandatory. Blocked by C (eager dispatch must exist for judgment to happen before ready).
